ud3.7:2.3: As told at [ud1.6:2.3](), Kassapa refused alms from the gods and visited poor areas, such as the streets of the embroiderers.
ud3.7:3.2: The _pesa_ was evidently gold-embroidered cloth. Of old, Indra was known for bearing gifts of such cloth (Rig Veda 1.61.16, 1.63.9). Here he is making _pesa_ together with his wife Sujā ([sn11.12:6.1]()). She spins the thread, while he embroiders the patterns. | The Pali’s _tantaṁ_ (“thread”) here echoes the verb _tanute_ (“one threads”) said of the _peśaskārī_ at Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 4.4.4, confirming that it is the same action described. There, one is said to embroider a figure such as a person.
ud3.7:3.6: I’m not sure if _anekarasabyañjano_ is correct, although the word does occur at [pv13:15.4]() and [pv27:12.4](). The commentary, while not definitive, suggests _anekasūpabyañjano_ (_anekehi sūpehi ceva byañjanehi ca_), which would be more idiomatic. However it is not attested.
